main_statement.paraphrase: For the Alt-Caffarelli one-phase energy int |grad v|^2 + 1_{v>0} with arbitrary nonnegative Sobolev competitors on balls, there is no singular minimizing cone in dimensions 5 or 6; together with Jerison-Savin (none in d<=4) and De Silva-Jerison (one exists in d=7), the critical dimension is exactly 7. The new content is the exclusion of d=5,6 (Thm 7.4 = cutoffs.tex:315-351). It is exactly the claim that d_* is the top value of the known range {5,6,7}.

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: Local minimizers: free boundary smooth outside Sing(u); Sing empty for n<=6, locally finite for n=7, dim_H Sing <= n-7 for n>=7, sharp (DJ cone x R^{n-7}).

relation_to_known_results: Caffarelli-Jerison-Kenig 2004: d_*>=4 (no stable smooth-link cones in R^3); conjectured flatness of stable cones for n<=6.
Jerison-Savin 2015: stable smooth-link cones flat for n<=4 => d_*>=5; their Sec 3.2 explains why Hessian-power tests fail in 4<=n<=6.
De Silva-Jerison 2009: nonflat minimizing cone in R^7 => d_*<=7.
Firester-Tsiamis-Wang 2026 (arXiv 2601.16966): symmetric (cohomogeneity-one) cones unstable n<=6, stable n>=7 - symmetric case only.
Fernandez-Real-Serra 2026 (arXiv 2609.05669): stable classical solutions in R^4 are 1D (removes homogeneity in d=4).
Mazzoleni-Tortone-Velichkov 2023 (arXiv 2310.06591): states d* in {5,6,7} as the open range.
Quick web search found no other claimed resolution of d_*=7.

proof_architecture.claim: Known bounds 5<=d_*<=7 (JS 2015; DJ 2009). Suppose d=d_* in {5,6}; fix a nonflat 1-homogeneous minimizer.
Minimal-dimension reduction: off-origin blowups are (d-1)-dimensional minimizers times R, hence flat; link components are smooth with Delta g=-mg, g=0, grad g=N; some component has T_o != 0.
If d=5, suspend to R^6 (minimality preserved), so in both cases the working link is Omega in S^5 (with two tips if suspended).
Spherical tensor identities, s^2<1, H>0, boundary jets; second variation gives stability int H v^2 <= int |grad v|^2+4v^2 on S^5.
Universal algebraic certificate (Prop 4.1) for free normalized jet data (A,p,g,X,w,z,ell).
Build h=w^a sqrt f and flux Z; fourth derivatives cancel; div Z >= 4h^2+|grad h|^2+eps w^{2a}; reflection parity gives N.Z+Hh^2 >= delta w^{2a+1}.
Exact verification of the certificate: Gram blocks PSD, graph calculus, graph bounds, 1714-key remainder dominated by 4x4 matrix with positive slacks; boundary reduces to 11 symmetric coefficients.

Cutoffs near Hessian zeros and tips: weighted Bochner integrability (a>1/2), integrated comparison, dominated convergence; positive mass int w^{2a} contradicts stability. Hence d_* not in {5,6}, so d_*=7.
Corollary: Weiss dimension reduction gives Sing empty n<=6, locally finite n=7, dim<=n-7, sharp via DJ x R^{n-7}.

eureka_candidates_ranked.item: P22 + P21 (flux pair (h,Z) with a universal SOS-type tensor certificate)
eureka_candidates_ranked.provisional_F: F3 (with F5: normalized jet representation P20)
for: Directly overcomes the obstruction JS 2015 Sec 3.2 identified for 4<=n<=6: the interior and boundary constraints on a single Hessian-power test are optimized by different configurations. Here a non-gradient flux Z decouples the two (interior: div Z; boundary: N.Z), so the same tensor data serve both.

Non-analytic: neither f,U,K,M,P nor Z occurs in the goal, in Mathlib, or in the bibliography; JS's tests are scalar functions of Hessian eigenvalues with the subsolution form (equivalent to Z = h grad h).
Load-bearing: the entire new half of the theorem (exclusion of d=5,6) rests on it; everything else is standard N0-N1.
Huge budget drop if it is right: a 40+-year-old style open problem (CJK conjecture n<=6 for minimizers) settled by a pointwise certificate plus routine cutoffs.
against: Paper names JS ('functions of the Hessian satisfying inequalities for the linearized free-boundary problem') and Simons as precedents; the vector-field form of a stability-violation certificate is the classical integration-by-parts / calibration idea.

The certificate is machine-found (SDP-style search over an ansatz); the human-level idea may be 'make the JS test function a general polynomial in (A,p,g), allow a flux, and let an SDP find it' - which is a natural move for an SOS-literate analyst.

SOS/auxiliary-function certificates for PDE inequalities exist in control theory (Valmorbida-Ahmadi-Papachristodoulou, arXiv 1703.06371; Chernyshenko et al.), so the method is transfer (N0 bridge) even if the specific certificate is new.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found on a full reading of the ~2,700 lines of LaTeX (excluding tables). The analytic skeleton (reductions, stability with Hardy constant 4, flux identity, boundary parity, cutoffs) checks line by line. The weight of the proof sits in Proposition 4.1, a large computer-verified certificate (231 + 557 table rows, 1714 interior keys) that we did not recompute. This is an extraordinary claim: it settles the open question d_* in {5,6,7} and, implicitly, the CJK stability conjecture for smooth-link cones in R^5, R^6. The Lean formalization does NOT cover any of the new mathematics.
checked: Suspension: tilde g = sin t g_o, tilde T = rho^{-1} T_o, |tilde B|^2 = rho^{-4}(|B_o|^2+3c^2 w_o^2), measures rho^4, rho^3 (geometry.tex:246-332): consistent with warped connection.

Stability: second variation with layer cancellation of normal-derivative terms gives int|grad phi|^2 >= int H phi^2 (geometry.tex:392-479), matches CJK/JS (2.4); Hardy constant ((m-1)/2)^2 = 4 for m=5.

Divergence identity: d/dl of w^{2a} G X gives (2a-1) q G X after X=B/w (flux.tex:137-158); U part: delta_li U_jk grad_l B_ijk = U:Delta T = 5 U:A w; skew part via commutator gives C(delta A + delta A) (flux.tex:75-95). Correct.
Square completion: f|l|^2 - F.l = f|l - F/2f|^2 - |F|^2/4f and |grad h|^2 = w^{2a}|F|^2/(4f) (flux.tex:160-191). Correct.
f >= eps_*: at X=w=z=0, |l|=1, all D-terms vanish and I=f (certificate-proof.tex:559-561). Correct.
Boundary: N.Z + H h^2 = w^{2a+1} S with P=0 at g=0 and Hh^2 = -lambda w^{2a+1} f (flux.tex:276-289). Correct.

Arithmetic re-checked here from printed integers: all ten D0 entries <= 2Q^2 Dbar (ratios 0.9992-0.99992, tight); slacks (673/18400, 438907/12000000, 2844869/24900000, 3479389/7600000) reproduce exactly; sum of the eleven boundary coefficients = 1656725282 and 1/4 - 1656725282/Q^2 = delta_* exactly.
Weighted Bochner: 2I <= (1/a) int Delta eta W^a + 4(1-a) I, 2-4(1-a) = 4a-2 = 8/25 > 0 needs a > 1/2 (cutoffs.tex:71-88). Correct.
Tip integrability: errors * s^4 <= C s^{2-2a} D_o, exponent 21/25 > -1; positive mass I_o int sin^{71/25} > 0 (cutoffs.tex:290-339). Correct.
Tensor bounds: ||A||_op^2 <= 4/5 and (tr A^3)^2 <= 9/20 for unit trace-free 5x5 A (Okumura-type) correct.
residual_concerns: Formula-to-code correspondence is not certified: the README says the finite checks 'do not certify equivalence between mathematical formulas and code, or the analytic proof'. An independent interior engine reproduced 1714/1714 keys (oracle-comparison.json), but both engines implement the same written decoding; a shared misreading of a contraction convention would propagate. Boundary verified by a separate script (boundary-independent.py). We did not execute repository code (untrusted-code policy) and did not recompute the expansion.
The margins are tight (D0/Dbar ratios up to 0.99992 after rounding to 1e-5), so any coefficient transcription error in Tables I/II could flip the conclusion.

Implied strength: the argument after Section 2 uses only stability and a smooth link (plus suspension), so it would prove the CJK stability conjecture for smooth-link cones in dims 5 and 6, which JS 2015 indicated their method could not reach. The paper does not state this; reviewers should check whether minimality is used anywhere beyond the reductions (we found no such use).

Suspension case: stability on the suspended cone is derived from minimality of the product (Prop 2.8) and tests supported away from the axis; the certificate needs s^2<1, H>0, w>0 which transfer from Omega_o. Fine as written; the axis is handled only by cutoffs, never by regularity.

Lean covers only the known De Silva-Jerison existence (comparator nonflat_in_seven, 13,545 lines), not the new exclusion; lean/docs/367.md says the flatness classification 'and the resulting regularity and singular-set bounds are outside this selected statement'.
How the certificate was found is not disclosed (no SDP solver, seeds or numerical precursor files are released).

extraction_friction: The headline's new half is not formalized: the comparator targets the known DJ existence. Any Lean-DAG load-bearing measure therefore says nothing about the paper's eureka candidates; the Lean DAG is a formalization of De Silva-Jerison 2009 (with formalization-specific explicit barriers).
